title: Same component, same spot: state stays

slides.say: You switch between two Counter tags, expecting a fresh counter. The score stays. Why?
Both branches render a Counter as the first child of the div. Same component, same position.

slides.text: React doesn’t see your if or ?: . It only sees the tree you return.
slides.say: React does not know where you put the conditions. It only sees the tree you return. To React, both are the first child of the first child of the root.

slides.text: Same type + same position = same component. Props change, state stays.
slides.say: So it is the same counter. The props change, but the state is preserved.
